peopleAlsoAsk.question: Can a pig survive CSF?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Some moderately virulent strains have caused only 20% mortality in experimentally infected pigs. Regardless of the virulence of the isolate, chronically infected animals and persistently infected piglets usually die. Persistently infected piglets, which are immunotolerant to CSFV, do not respond to CSF vaccines.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What are the symptoms of the porcine virus?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Pigs affected may experience increased mortality, poor growth, and weight loss, progressing to the level of severe thinning, and weakness between 5 to 14 weeks of age. Also pigs can develop enlarged lymph nodes, skin rashes, difficulty breathing, jaundice, fever, stomach ulcers, diarrhea, or sudden death may occur.
